title: The Cartesian core of a Cartesian fibration is a right fibration
statement: Use quasicategories, cores and coherent functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and Cartesian fibrations, Cartesian edges, right fibrations and degreewise fibers of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Work in a fixed containing universe. Let $p:E\to B$ be a Cartesian fibration between quasicategories. Let $E^{\mathrm{cart}}\subseteq E$ consist of the simplices all of whose edges are $p$-Cartesian. Then $p|_{E^{\mathrm{cart}}}:E^{\mathrm{cart}}\to B$ is a right fibration. For every vertex $b$ of $B$, its degreewise fiber is the core $(E_b)^{\simeq}$ of the original fiber. Under this identification, right-fibration transport along $f:b\to c$ is the restriction to cores of Cartesian transport $f^*:E_c\to E_b$.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.2.5, printed p. 122, with Proposition 2.4.1.5 for Cartesian edges over identities and the fiber-core identification; no Stacks tag.

proof.text: The simplicial subset $E^{\mathrm{cart}}$ is closed under faces and degeneracies: every edge of a face of a simplex is an edge of that simplex, and every edge of a degeneracy $s_j\sigma$ is an edge of $\sigma$ or a degenerate edge, and degenerate edges are $p$-Cartesian by the Cartesian dual (through [lem-coef-marked-opposite-relative-calculus], which exchanges cartesian and cocartesian edges under $E\mapsto E^{\mathrm{op}}$, $B\mapsto B^{\mathrm{op}}$) of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. The same dual gives, for a $2$-simplex of $E$ with edges $u:x\to y$, $v:y\to z$, $w:x\to z$ and $v$ $p$-Cartesian, that $u$ is $p$-Cartesian if and only if $w$ is (composition and cancellation). Now take a lifting problem $\Lambda_i^n\to E^{\mathrm{cart}}$ over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to B$ with $n\ge1$, $0<i\le n$. Case $n=1$, $i=1$: the horn is a vertex $y$ over $\sigma(1)$, and the Cartesian-fibration clause of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] gives a $p$-Cartesian edge over $\sigma$ with target $y$; it lies in $E^{\mathrm{cart}}$. Case $n\ge2$, $0<i<n$: $p$ is an inner fibration, so a filler $\Delta^n\to E$ over $\sigma$ exists. Case $n\ge2$, $i=n$: the edge $\{n-1,n\}$ lies in the face $d_0$ of $\Lambda^n_n$, so it is prescribed and $p$-Cartesian, and by the definition of a $p$-Cartesian edge in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] a filler over $\sigma$ exists. It remains to see that every edge of the filler is Cartesian. For $n\ge3$ every edge $\{a,b\}$ of $\Delta^n$ misses at least two vertices, hence a vertex $j\neq i$, so it lies in the face $d_j\subseteq\Lambda_i^n$ and is already Cartesian. For $n=2$, $i=1$, the only new edge is $\{0,2\}$, the composite in a $2$-simplex whose edges $\{0,1\},\{1,2\}$ are Cartesian, hence Cartesian; for $n=2$, $i=2$, the only new edge is $\{0,1\}$, and $\{1,2\},\{0,2\}$ are Cartesian, so cancellation makes $\{0,1\}$ Cartesian. Hence the filler lies in $E^{\mathrm{cart}}$ and $p|_{E^{\mathrm{cart}}}$ is a right fibration. Since $B$ is a quasicategory and $p|_{E^{\mathrm{cart}}}$ lifts inner horns, $E^{\mathrm{cart}}$ is a quasicategory as well.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.2.5 and Proposition 2.4.1.5, printed p. 122; the outer-horn proof that the Cartesian-edge simplicial subset is a right fibration.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $b$ of $B$. A simplex of the degreewise fiber $E^{\mathrm{cart}}\times_B\{b\}$ is a simplex of $E_b=E\times_B\{b\}$ all of whose edges are $p$-Cartesian; each such edge lies over the degenerate edge $\mathrm{id}_b$. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-local-global] to the inner fibration $p^{\mathrm{op}}:E^{\mathrm{op}}\to B^{\mathrm{op}}$; by [lem-coef-marked-opposite-relative-calculus] its cocartesian edges are the $p$-Cartesian edges reversed, and its vertex fibers are the opposites $(E_b)^{\mathrm{op}}$. The hypothesis of its degenerate-base clause holds because the degenerate edge at the source is cocartesian ([lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]). Since an edge of $E_b$ is an equivalence exactly when its reverse is an equivalence of $(E_b)^{\mathrm{op}}$, an edge of $E_b$ is $p$-Cartesian if and only if it is an equivalence in $E_b$. Therefore the degreewise fiber is exactly the simplicial subset of $E_b$ of simplices all of whose edges are equivalences, which is the core $(E_b)^{\simeq}$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The identification is an equality of simplicial subsets of $E$, and holds trivially when $E_b$ is empty. As a consistency check, $E^{\mathrm{cart}}$ is a quasicategory (step 1), so [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] applied to the right fibration $p|_{E^{\mathrm{cart}}}$ also gives that this fiber is a Kan complex.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.5 and Corollary 2.4.2.5, printed p. 122; fiber-core identification.

proof.text: Let $f:b\to c$ be an edge of $B$. Cartesian transport along $f$ is the end map $h_0=h|_{\{0\}\times E_c}:E_c\to E_b$ of a map $h:\Delta^1\times E_c\to E$ with $ph=f\circ\mathrm{pr}_{\Delta^1}$, $h|_{\{1\}\times E_c}$ the inclusion, and every edge $h|_{\Delta^1\times\{y\}}$ $p$-Cartesian; right-fibration transport along $f$ for $p|_{E^{\mathrm{cart}}}$ is the end map of a map $g:\Delta^1\times(E^{\mathrm{cart}})_c\to E^{\mathrm{cart}}$ over $f\circ\mathrm{pr}_{\Delta^1}$ with $g|_{\{1\}\times(E^{\mathrm{cart}})_c}$ the inclusion. Given such an $h$, by step 2 $(E^{\mathrm{cart}})_c=(E_c)^{\simeq}$; restrict $h$ to $g=h|_{\Delta^1\times(E_c)^{\simeq}}$. We check that $g$ lands in $E^{\mathrm{cart}}$, i.e. that every edge of $\Delta^1\times(E_c)^{\simeq}$ goes to a $p$-Cartesian edge. An edge is $(\alpha,e)$ with $\alpha$ an edge of $\Delta^1$ and $e:y\to y'$ an equivalence of $E_c$ (or degenerate). If $\alpha$ is constant at $1$, its image is $e$, an equivalence over $\mathrm{id}_c$, hence $p$-Cartesian by step 2. If $\alpha$ is constant at $0$, its image is $h_0(e)$; the simplicial map $h_0:E_c\to E_b$ carries the inverse and the two $2$-simplex witnesses of $e$ to such data for $h_0(e)$, so $h_0(e)$ is an equivalence of $E_b$ and hence $p$-Cartesian by step 2. If $\alpha$ is $0\to1$ and $e$ is degenerate at $y$, the image is $h|_{\Delta^1\times\{y\}}$, Cartesian by hypothesis. If $\alpha$ is $0\to1$ and $e$ is arbitrary, the $2$-simplex $((0,1,1),s_0e)$ of $\Delta^1\times(E_c)^{\simeq}$ has edges $(0\to1,\mathrm{id}_y)$, $(1,e)$ and $(0\to1,e)$; its image is a $2$-simplex of $E$ whose first two edges are Cartesian by the previous cases, so its third edge is Cartesian by the composition law of step 1 ([lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], dualized by [lem-coef-marked-opposite-relative-calculus]). Hence $g$ is a map into $E^{\mathrm{cart}}$ over $f\circ\mathrm{pr}_{\Delta^1}$ restricting to the inclusion of the fiber at $1$, i.e. a right-fibration transport datum along $f$, and its end map is $h_0|_{(E_c)^{\simeq}}:(E_c)^{\simeq}\to(E_b)^{\simeq}$, the restriction to cores of Cartesian transport. On vertices this sends $y$ to the source of the Cartesian lift $h|_{\Delta^1\times\{y\}}$ of $f$ with target $y$.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.2.5 with Proposition 2.4.1.5, printed p. 122; transport and compatibility with Cartesian transport.

proof.text: Steps 1 to 3 together give all three clauses: $p|_{E^{\mathrm{cart}}}$ is a right fibration, its degreewise fiber over each vertex $b$ is $(E_b)^{\simeq}$, and every Cartesian transport datum along $f$ restricts on cores to a right-fibration transport datum with end map the restriction of $f^*$. No step used a size bound beyond the fixed universe of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] or nonemptiness of any fiber.
